title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lansing, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lansing, OH
metaDescription: Lansing sits in Belmont County, in one of Ohio's most active Utica/Point Pleasant drilling corridors. See what that means for your mineral value.
heroLead: Lansing sits in a part of Belmont County that ran on coal mining for generations, and shale drilling has layered right on top of that older history in the years since.
intro: Lansing is a small village in Belmont County, one of the most heavily developed counties in Ohio's Utica/Point Pleasant play. Coal mining defined this area's economy for most of the 20th century, and many of the mineral reservations around Lansing trace back to coal-company or farm-family deeds written decades before anyone drilled a horizontal well into the Point Pleasant formation beneath them.

sections.heading: What Belmont County's development history means for Lansing
paragraphs: Belmont County has consistently ranked among Ohio's most active Utica/Point Pleasant counties, and a tract near Lansing has a real chance of already sitting inside a producing spacing unit. Royalty statements or division orders, where they exist, give the clearest and most reliable path to an accurate valuation.

sections.heading: Untangling coal and oil and gas severances
paragraphs: Because coal was frequently severed separately from oil and gas in this area, confirming exactly what your family's mineral reservation covers requires reading the actual recorded severance deed at the Belmont County Recorder's office in St. Clairsville. Once that's clear, checking for any lease or unitization order tied to your specific tract completes the picture.

faqs.question: Is Lansing in a heavily drilled part of Belmont County?
faqs.answer: Much of Belmont County has seen dense Utica/Point Pleasant development, and Lansing sits within that broader activity, though results vary by specific spacing unit.

faqs.question: Could coal and oil and gas rights on my family's land be owned by different parties?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common here. The original severance deed will specify what was reserved and to whom, which is worth confirming before assuming who owns what.

faqs.question: What if my family's minerals have never generated a royalty check?
faqs.answer: Your interest may sit in a unit that hasn't started producing yet, or you may not be properly identified on the current division order. A title search will clarify which situation applies.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting a buyer?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them, which together establish your net mineral acres and current decimal interest.

faqs.question: Do I need to sell my entire mineral interest, or can I sell a portion?
faqs.answer: Most owners can sell all or part of their net mineral acres, sometimes limiting a sale to the interest under one well or unit while retaining the rest, depending on how the chain of title is structured.
